1: The patient's symptoms of a slowly growing, dull, intermittent swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule, along with the presence of a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa, are consistent with a periapical abscess. The panoramic radiography demonstrating a mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices further supports this diagnosis.
2: The patient's symptoms and examination findings, including the presence of a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa, are consistent with a periapical granuloma. The provisional diagnosis of periapical granuloma was made based on the clinical presentation and radiographic findings.
